# build_unified_ontology { #dyf.build_unified_ontology }

```python
build_unified_ontology(
    embeddings,
    main_similarity_threshold=0.55,
    outlier_similarity_threshold=0.45,
    diversity_gap_threshold=0.02,
    outlier_diversity_gap=0.015,
    k_neighbors=30,
    verbose=False,
)
```

Build a unified ontology that covers both dense and sparse embedding regions.

Uses a two-tier approach:
1. Build main ontology with high similarity threshold (dense regions)
2. Build outlier ontology with lower threshold (sparse regions)
3. Add bridge edges to connect them
4. Exclude "double outliers" that don't fit either

This achieves ~96% coverage vs ~89% for single-threshold approach.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name                         | Type                                     | Description                                               | Default    |
|------------------------------|------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| embeddings                   | [np](`numpy`).[ndarray](`numpy.ndarray`) | Embeddings to analyze (n, d). Will be L2-normalized.      | _required_ |
| main_similarity_threshold    | [float](`float`)                         | Similarity threshold for main ontology (default 0.55).    | `0.55`     |
| outlier_similarity_threshold | [float](`float`)                         | Similarity threshold for outlier ontology (default 0.45). | `0.45`     |
| diversity_gap_threshold      | [float](`float`)                         | Diversity gap for main ontology edges (default 0.02).     | `0.02`     |
| outlier_diversity_gap        | [float](`float`)                         | Diversity gap for outlier ontology edges (default 0.015). | `0.015`    |
| k_neighbors                  | [int](`int`)                             | Number of neighbors for k-NN graph.                       | `30`       |
| verbose                      | [bool](`bool`)                           | Print progress information.                               | `False`    |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                     | Description                                                |
|--------|----------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [UnifiedOntologyResult](`dyf.rag.UnifiedOntologyResult`) | UnifiedOntologyResult with combined ontology and metadata. |

## Example {.doc-section .doc-section-example}

>>> from dyf import build_unified_ontology
>>>
>>> result = build_unified_ontology(embeddings, verbose=True)
>>> print(result.summary())
>>>
>>> # Access the unified ontology
>>> ontology = result.ontology
>>> ancestors = ontology.get_ancestors(node_idx)
>>>
>>> # Check which tier a node came from
>>> if node_idx in result.main_nodes:
...     print("From main ontology")
>>> elif node_idx in result.outlier_nodes:
...     print("From outlier ontology")
